approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `value` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

name().details: Returns the name of the token.

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

proxiableUUID().details: Implementation of the ERC-1822 {proxiableUUID} function. This returns the storage slot used by the implementation. It is used to validate the implementation's compatibility when performing an upgrade. IMPORTANT: A proxy pointing at a proxiable contract should not be considered proxiable itself, because this risks bricking a proxy that upgrades to it, by delegating to itself until out of gas. Thus it is critical that this function revert if invoked through a proxy. This is guaranteed by the `notDelegated` modifier.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes).details: Upgrade the implementation of the proxy to `newImplementation`, and subsequently execute the function call encoded in `data`. Calls {_authorizeUpgrade}. Emits an {Upgraded} event.

Independent grants, pauses, canonical calldata and value controls remain required. Require zero native value for these BNB Chain ERC20 flows; deposit ABI is payable but native funding is not supported by the reviewed sUSD1+ override.

BNB Chain sUSD1+ proxy 0x4F2760B32720F013E900DC92F65480137391199b currently resolves through ERC1967/UUPS to sUSD1PlusVault implementation 0x972c27EE69B19D7648cef365700c22713A9a31fd. Implementation source-service runtime exact_match; proxy generic-bytecode source is match only with no creation match, not relabeled exact and not used as protocol implementation ABI. Manager can upgrade future behavior.

underlying is USD1 0x8d0D000Ee44948FC98c9B98A4FA4921476f08B0d, observed through proxy getter; selected financial amounts are token base units and shares have 18 decimals with Precision=1e18. Accepted alternative ERC20s are manager-configured and normalized only by decimal count, not price/swapping. Do not treat USDT/USDC equivalence, fee-on-transfer behavior or changing accept list as guaranteed.

deposit pulls underlyingToken from msg.sender using allowance to vault, first into vault then onward to first configured custody portfolio (Ceffu wallet in source comments). It DOES NOT immediately mint usable shares: floor(alignedAmount*1e18/currentUnitNav) is added to caller pendingShares for current settlement period. Administrator-authorized KYT confirmation is separate and requires an EIP712 signature. confirmShare/refundShare signatures are deliberately excluded; this catalog does not promise a complete pending-deposit confirmation/refund workflow or ability to access funds.

deposit is payable at ABI level but reviewed override uses IERC20 transfers even for NATIVE_TOKEN sentinel and never wraps BNB. Extra msg.value on an ERC20 deposit is not forwarded/refunded and can remain trapped. Use accepted real ERC20 addresses with exactly zero native value. No caller-selected recipient or arbitrary strategy/execution payload exists.

requestWithdraw uses caller own usable shares after frozen shares and already queued withdrawals; zero is rejected, configured minimum applies unless withdrawing entire usable balance. Repeated requests in the same settlement period merge under requestId=settlementPeriod; requestTimestamp is refreshed. Shares remain in wallet balance but cannot be spent while queued. No immediate payout, cancellation, caller-defined minimum output or deadline is supplied.

withdraw(requestId) requires requestId+1 < settlementPeriod and an unexecuted request belonging to msg.sender. It removes queued accounting, burns requested shares and transfers only configured underlying USD1 to msg.sender. NAV used is getUnitNav(requestId+1), i.e. periodUnitNav[requestId], and floor(shares*unitNav/1e18) applies. Two manager period advances are required, not an enforced wall-clock settlement deadline. Treasury must actually hold enough USD1; custodied funds are not pulled back automatically by this method.

Primary March 2026 redemption guide describes estimated 3-6 days, variable settlement NAV, and claim step; this timing is not guaranteed by contract and large requests/other conditions can extend it. Guide quotes 35% management/performance fees; selected source has no per-call fee parameter/deduction and relies on administered NAV/custody accounting. Fee basis/current prospectus must be checked rather than inferred from source.

Selected retail deposit/request/withdraw enforce pause, caller-blacklist and reentrancy checks; manager can set/reset NAV (including prior periods), accepted underlying, portfolios, minimums, freeze balances, blacklist users, set transferability, signers and upgrade implementation. Investor exposure includes offchain CeFi strategies, custody, CEX and law-enforcement restrictions, not isolated onchain asset backing or guaranteed recovery.

Current official product guide explicitly geo-restricts several jurisdictions including US, Canada, China and Netherlands and says list is nonexhaustive and mutable. KYT, app terms, sanctions and jurisdictional eligibility remain external restrictions. No exemption or eligibility clearance is implied. No raw arbitrary executor, management, signature approval, bridge, share burn or alternate unguarded BN-wallet entrypoint is admitted.
